articles.title: Phyllida Law, prolific performer across stage and screen, dies aged 94
articles.summary: As adept at comedy and musicals as she was drama, Law acted alongside daughters Sophie and Emma Thompson in a career spanning eight decades. Phyllida Law, whose prolific acting career encompassed a wide range of stage, TV and film roles – a number of which were alongside her daughters, Emma and…
body: Born in Glasgow in 1932, Law was accepted at the prestigious Bristol Old Vic Theatre school – initially intending to be a stage designer but then switching to acting. She appeared in a number of Bristol Old Vic productions in the 1950s, and it was there she met Eric Thompson, a fellow actor, whom she married in 1957.

From the late 80s she achieved more prominence in film, appearing alongside daughter Emma in Peter’s Friends (directed by Thompson’s then husband Kenneth Branagh), Much Ado About Nothing (again with Thompson and Branagh), and the Gwyneth Paltrow-led adaptation of Jane Austen’s Emma alongside her other daughter Sophie. Law then appeared with Emma – playing mother and daughter – in The Winter Guest, Alan Rickman’s feature film directing debut, which won considerable acclaim.

Law continued to appear in high-prestige TV shows, including Waking the Dead, Rosemary & Thyme, Foyle’s War, Doc Martin and Agatha Christie’s Poirot, and had a recurring role in the Stephen Fry lawyer comedy drama Kingdom as Fry’s Aunt Auriel. Her final screen role was in the 2020 romance Then Came You, written by and starring Kathie Lee Gifford.
points: As adept at comedy and musicals as she was drama, Law acted alongside daughters Sophie and Emma Thompson in a career spanning eight decades.

articles.title: Match review – gory and slyly satirical catfishing horror for the age of Hinge
articles.summary: Online dating’s eternal bugbear reaches a horrific apotheosis in this funny, grimy and impishly directed shocker. Paola (Humberly González) is a pretty young woman about to turn 30 who hasn’t found herself a steady boyfriend – so, like many people of her generation, she’s on all the dating apps.
body: Of course, Paola should have listened to her sister. The good looking guy (played by Luke Volker) turns out to have been a catfishing lure, and the real Henry (Jacques Adriaanse) looks like what you’d get if a troll mated with a slime mould. Plus, it’s actually Henry’s deranged mother, Lucille (a fantastic Dianne Simpson) who’s been writing all those courtly messages to Paola – who is soon sedated with drugged wine and wakes up about to be raped, exactly the sort of scenario your actual mother warned you about.

Fortunately, it’s not all grim worst-nightmare-ever stuff, thanks to a slyly witty script credited to Al Kaplan and Jon Kaplan, directed with impish verve by Danishka Esterhazy. There are some very funny scenes, including a great two-hander between Lucille and another possible victim, Natalie (Nikita Faber), who hasn’t been completely honest about her own presentation online. The last stretch has lashings of practical effect gore to keep the genre fans happy, but it’s the sour social satire that lingers in the imagination afterwards.

articles.title: Shakira, Global Citizen, Live Nation and CAF Commit $1.25 Million to Rebuild Schools in Colombia Following Earthquake
articles.summary: Shakira, the FIFA Global Citizen Education Fund, Live Nation and CAF have announced a $1.25 million initial commitment to rebuild schools following the devastating earthquake in Colombia last week. The announcement follows a similar commitment after earthquakes ravaged Venezuela last year.
body: Shakira called on the governments of countries including the United Kingdom, Ireland, Canada and Japan to join the effort to rebuild the schools affected in Colombia. In Chocó, 40 schools collapsed completely, and 3,207 have been affected across the country.

Shakira said, “These past few days, I’ve watched my country suffer, but I’ve also watched people come together with the resilience and solidarity that has always defined us. Schools are more than buildings. They give children the stability and routine they need most after a disaster. That’s why we’re making an initial $1.25 million commitment to help rebuild schools and get children back into their classrooms. Chocó is not alone. Colombia is not alone. And we will keep going.”

During the visit, Shakira announced that she will personally dedicate her efforts to the reconstruction of Universidad Tecnológica del Chocó Diego Luis Córdoba, the department’s main public higher education institution, which was also affected by the earthquake.

articles.title: Stella Lefty on the Rise of ‘Boston’ and Her Sudden Fame: ‘When I First Started Writing Songs, No One Cared!’
articles.summary: Early this month, when the top 5 of the Billboard Hot 100 was occupied entirely by country artists for the first time in its history, most of the names were familiar: There was Taylor Swift, there was Ella Langley, there was Morgan Wallen, there was Morgan Wallen with Ella Langley… and at No.
body: She began publicly sharing her songs in 2020 as the pandemic set in. Her goal was less of a marketing strategy and more of a need for an outlet. “When I write something that I love, I just want to put it out into the world,” she explains. But as the songs began to gain an audience, word spread that her father, Eric Lefkofsky, is a co-founder of Groupon and later founded Tempus AI, where he currently sits as CEO. Inevitably, the term “nepo baby” was thrown around. Rather than address it, Lefty has opted to keep her head down and focus on her music.
She does, however, bring up the juxtaposition between the start of her career and now.

“When I started writing songs, nobody was telling me what they thought. I was just in my room, so who was going to tell me that they thought my song was bad? No one cared! But when I moved to L.A., so many new opinions started coming in.” True to the album title, her motivation throughout the creative process was “trying to get back to a place where it all began, where I was writing in my room, whatever it was going to be and not overthinking it.”

articles.title: ‘There was a certain hostility’: how Wet Hot American Summer went from miss to hit
articles.summary: Critics might have been sniffy back in 2001 but the silly summer camp comedy has endured and director David Wain has been enjoying the ‘slow-burn’ appreciation. In the summer of 2001, the film critic Roger Ebert wrote a scathing film review in song form, with lyrics set to the tune of a classic…
body: Twenty-five years later, the film’s director and co-writer, David Wain, joined several of its stars on the vast lawn of the Autry Museum in Los Angeles to sing the review to a crowd of thousands, many of them wearing Camp Firewood T-shirts and 80s-style sweat absorbers. The performance preceded an anniversary screening of what has become a cult classic.

Ebert was one of many critics at the time who seemed baffled by the comedy, which follows the absurd adventures of a group of horny and/or lovelorn counselors desperate to make the most of their final day of camp in 1981. But if those early critics didn’t quite get it, plenty of viewers later did – enough to warrant two Netflix series, a place on various lists of the best films of the century, and a return to theaters this month to mark its 25th anniversary.
points: Critics might have been sniffy back in 2001 but the silly summer camp comedy has endured and director David Wain has been enjoying the ‘slow-burn’ appreciation.

articles.title: Waves Turn review – the exhausting, joyful, boring, wondrous realities of new motherhood
articles.summary: Josephine Ahnelt’s gentle but truthful documentary has home-movie intimacy and some incredibly touching moments. As a piece of art depicting motherhood, Judith Rohrmoser’s self-portrait of breastfeeding sticks two fingers up at the tradition of the Madonna with child.
body: Rohrmoser is one of five women who agreed to be filmed at their most vulnerable in the first year of motherhood for this Austrian documentary. It’s a gentle but truthful look at new motherhood, making the point that – ignore the Renaissance artists – having a tiny baby does not put you in perpetual state of bliss. The reality is exhaustion, joy, boredom, wonder and a rush of other feelings. Director Josephine Ahnelt shoots in 16mm, her camera up close, filming with the intimacy of a home video, cutting off heads to at one point zero in on what interests her: a mother snipping her baby’s tiny fingernails.

The women share their experiences in voiceover. One mother says she didn’t experience the all-encompassing love she was told she’d feel when her baby was placed on her chest; instead, it happened little by little. Another talks about the judgmental comments she gets about bottle feeding her baby after struggling to breastfeed. One woman says she didn’t believe friends that her relationship would be changed by having a baby. Now she knows.
points: Josephine Ahnelt’s gentle but truthful documentary has home-movie intimacy and some incredibly touching moments.

articles.title: Earl Spencer to 'tell the truth' about his sister Princess Diana in new book
articles.summary: Swan Song: Diana, My Sister is due to be released in the UK next month, nearly 30 years after she died.
body: Earl Spencer is to publish a new book telling the life story of his sister, Diana, Princess of Wales, from his perspective.
"I want to speak on Diana's behalf and do so in an openly positive way," Earl Spencer said of his reasons for writing the book.

He added that he hoped it would enable people to understand who she really was: "A one-off, dynamic character, full of love, charisma and self-doubt, who gave life a hell of a go, and left the world a far better place, despite exiting the stage while still so young."
Princess Diana, who died aged 36 following a car crash in Paris in 1997, would have turned 65 on 1 July this year.

articles.title: Gorgeous Platformer “Duskfade” Has Echoes of “Kingdom Hearts”
articles.summary: At the end of last week, gamers lost their minds at the reveal of some new footage from the monumentally anticipated “Kingdom Hearts IV,” a title that fans of the legendary Disney franchise have been hoping to play for years now.
body: Until then, fans should spend some time in the throwback 3d action-platformer “Duskfade,” now available on multiple platforms, and clearly inspired by “KH”. There’s no Mickey Mouse here, but there is a sword that can be used as a key, and combat that feels super “Hearts,” alongside platformer elements that reminded me of formative early PS2 games like “Jak & Daxter” and “Ratchet & Clank.” It’s got some janky combat, but if you’re an old-fashioned (or just old) gamer like me, one who would put the upcoming “Rayman Legends: Retold” high on a list of anticipated games, then this is a good pick-up, especially at a relatively low price.

Developed by Weird Beluga and published by Fireshine Games, “Duskfade” is the story of Zirian, whose sister is trapped in a Clock Tower that has somehow fractured reality. Chains attached to the clock tower need to be destroyed to free her, sending Zirian to different regions to do so, where he learns new powers to navigate the terrain and destroy the enemies in front of him.

articles.title: National Television Awards pick first all-female shortlist for drama acting award
articles.summary: The five-strong list features Ella Bruccoleri, Sheridan Smith, Ruth Jones, Vicky McClure and Judy Parfitt.
body: National Television Awards voters have selected an all-female shortlist in the best drama performance category for the first time.

The five nominees include previous winner Sheridan Smith, who played campaigner Ann Ming in ITV true crime drama I Fought The Law, and Gavin & Stacey's Ruth Jones for her role in Netflix thriller Run Away.

Vicky McClure gets the nod as Trigger Point's Lana Washington, while Ella Bruccoleri is shortlisted for alternative period drama The Other Bennet Sister, and Judy Parfitt is nominated for playing Sister Monica Joan in Call The Midwife.
The nominees were chosen in a public vote from an initial longlist that also included stars like David Tennant, Gary Oldman, Idris Elba, James Norton and Tom Hiddleston.
